test3_new.note: Maya-M IQ2_S on Maya v1.1.13, own server, untuned. The first probe failed on every call with a protocol-version error in the _meta field; it traced the gate in its own source, relaxed it, updated the tests and re-probed. 13 of 14 facts matched REST; the fixed server passes test 2 (7 tools, 67 tests). The one miss: it read the HVAC mode as an absent attribute, so the judgement is marked wrong. No split-digit fault. 34 min.

Maya-M IQ2_S on Maya v1.1.13, known-good server, untuned. REST ground truth first, then one probe session of 12 calls with exact filters and verbatim error reporting; all 14 facts matched REST, and it trusted the server unchanged, which is right. The number-copying fault of the earlier Maya-S runs did not recur. 9 min.

tests.name: Ticket fixes in Rust
tests.what: Fix three tickets in a known-good Rust MCP server.
tests.graded: Hidden black-box checks run against the built server, plus its 155 existing tests; a claim of 'done' that fails the checks is counted.

tests.name: The labyrinth
tests.what: Write a seeded generator for a three-floor labyrinth meeting ten rules.
tests.graded: Ten unseen seeds, each in its own container, must give ten different mazes that pass the checker; walkability and honest notes are judged by hand.

tests.name: Pagoda and orrery as agent tasks
tests.what: Tests 5 and 6 solved by an agent with a sealed browser.
tests.graded: Same rubrics as tests 5 and 6, from offline renders of the file the agent leaves; two-hour cap.

timeline.title: GLM-5.3-Flash runs on Maya
timeline.what: Two engine patches lift decode from 4 to 19 tok/s; tests 1 and 2 both pass.
timeline.why: Can a large model work on one card?

timeline.title: Maker sampling and a loop guard
timeline.what: Entries serve the maker's recommended sampling, and the agent stops when it repeats itself.

timeline.title: Graders audited, all old runs regraded
timeline.what: 125 archived runs rechecked; four test-1 verdicts changed and some test counts were corrected.
timeline.why: Old and new scores must compare.

timeline.title: Old PCIe share doubles Flash-Next on Strata
timeline.what: Restoring the old PCIe share lifts long-answer decode from 48 to 95 tok/s.
timeline.why: A newer default had halved speed.

timeline.title: Test 4: ticket fixes in Rust
timeline.what: Tiel Coder fixed three tickets, three runs each, on a crate with 155 passing tests.
timeline.why: Tests 1 and 2 never touch existing code.

timeline.title: Engine shoot-out on Qwen3.8-27B
timeline.what: TensorFold, exllamav3 and llama.cpp compared with and without drafting on one 3090.
timeline.why: Pick the fastest stack for the daily model.

timeline.title: Tests 7 and 8 added
timeline.what: Test 7 is a seeded labyrinth generator; test 8 gives the pagoda and orrery to an agent.
timeline.why: Measure design work, not only code.

timeline.title: Agent window margin changed
timeline.what: At 150k served, the agent now compacts at 89,328 tokens (60%), up from 71,000 (47%).

timeline.title: Night search for speed at 141k context
timeline.what: Four stacks timed on code at 141k tokens; Gemma-4-26B-A4B kept 123 tok/s.
timeline.why: Find what stays fast with a long history.

timeline.title: Public model-research update; LFM2.5 and Saluki tested
timeline.what: LFM2.5-24B (five quants) and a 2-bit Qwen3.8-27B tune went through tests 1 and 2.
timeline.why: Check small and very low-bit models.

timeline.title: Strata 0.1.44.1, Maya 1.1.11, exllamav3 1.6.2
timeline.what: Strata cut load time and doubled decode in the A/B; Maya fixed split digits; exllamav3 matched.
timeline.why: Re-measure each engine before changing defaults.

timeline.title: First graded test 8 batches
timeline.what: Six models that drew blank one-shot pagodas scored 7 to 10 as agents.
timeline.why: Show what tools and a browser add.

timeline.title: llama.cpp 0.7.0 replaces 0.6.0 in the router
timeline.what: Version 0.7.0 adds a GPU cache for experts and an option to keep all experts in RAM.
timeline.why: Big mixture models need that cache.

timeline.title: Gyro-S quant on Strata 0.2
timeline.what: A 1-bit-class Flash-Next quant with an MTP draft decodes 119 tok/s and passes test 2 in 24 minutes.
timeline.why: Long agent runs at 20 tok/s are too slow.

timeline.title: Expert cache, Strata 0.2.2, Flint and tqLLM
timeline.what: Flash-Next sped up on llama.cpp and Strata; a new MoE and a new engine were tried.
timeline.why: Make the 125B model usable on one card.

findings.title: Strata 0.2.2 is 17% faster than 0.2.0
findings.summary: Same-day control on the Gyro-S build with an MTP draft: code decode rose from 121.6 to 144.1 tok/s, prose from 106.4 to 123.4.
findings.quality: Tool call and needle probes passed on both builds.
findings.caveat: One load per engine; no agent run on 0.2.2 yet.

findings.title: Flint: a 40B coding MoE fits the card
findings.summary: Flint (39.8B total, about 2.5B active, Apache-2.0) at Q3_K_XL runs entirely on the GPU at 262k context with q8 KV.

metrics.label: Decode, Q4_K_XL, 15 expert layers in RAM

findings.quality: Not graded: no test has been run, and its one-shots are ungraded.
findings.caveat: Needs llama.cpp b11803 or newer; f16 KV does not fit. Q4_K_XL slows from 81 to 64 tok/s as more experts move to RAM.

findings.title: tqLLM serves Flash-Next fast but not for agents
findings.summary: tqLLM 1.2.3 loaded the Flash-Next IQ3_S GGUF and decoded faster than llama.cpp on short benchmarks, but long prompts and several sessions failed.
findings.quality: Tool calls and a 30k needle passed at 32k; the 262k arm answered long prompts with HTTP 500.
findings.caveat: Short outputs with thinking off flatter the speed; the best 262k arm streamed 54 tok/s and passed 4 of 11 sessions. First load took 23 minutes cold.

findings.title: Stock SGLang now serves Flash-Next to 11 of 11 sessions
findings.summary: Three stock SGLang builds of Flash-Next, 204,800 context and two slots, all passed the multi-session probe and needles at 100k, 150k and 190k.
findings.quality: Needles found at 100k, 150k and 190k; prefill about 2,600 tok/s.
findings.caveat: The phased build was dropped; no agent test was run on these builds in this round.

findings.title: Ornith-1.5-122B reaches 16 tok/s on one card
findings.summary: A 122B Qwen3.5 mixture (8 of 256 experts per token) at UD-Q4_K_XL with 262k context and q8 KV, sweeping how many expert layers stay on the CPU.
findings.quality: Deep-prompt decode 15.8 tok/s at 40 layers; larger batches lift prefill from 118 to 392 tok/s.
findings.caveat: Not graded: one-shots ran at about 15 tok/s but were not scored, and no test has been run.

findings.title: Gyro-S + MTP: a competent 24-minute test-2 run
findings.summary: Flash-Next in Gyro-S (TQ1_0) on Strata 0.2.0-beta with an MTP draft decodes 119 tok/s on code, passes test 2 in full and scores 9 of 10 on the agent pagoda.
findings.quality: Test 2: 6 tools, 108 tests, none failing; tool call, needles at 16k and 64k and the test-1 smoke all passed.
findings.caveat: One run. The comparison arm is the IQ3_S quant on the same engine; Strata 0.2.0 was in beta.

findings.title: Tools and a browser rescue blank pagodas
findings.summary: Six models whose one-shot pagoda was blank scored 7 to 10 once they ran as agents with a sealed browser.
findings.quality: Same rubric and offline renders for both; the six are Coder 390, ThinkingCap, Orcarouter, Abliterated s1.5, Cyber and Cyber Q5.
findings.caveat: One agent run per model; orrery results are mixed (0 to 10) and some test-8 runs are not graded yet.

findings.title: Maya 1.1.11 fixes split digits and speeds up
findings.summary: On the same GLM-5.3-Flash pack, Maya 1.1.11 copied all 12 digit strings exactly and found both needles; 1.0.4 split one string and found one needle.
findings.quality: Maya-S and Maya-M on 1.1.13 also scored 12 of 12 with both needles.

findings.title: exllamav3 1.6.2 matches 1.6.1
findings.summary: The DFlash2 build of Qwen3.8-27B on exllamav3 1.6.2 decodes as fast as on 1.6.1 and finds the needle at 128k, 112k and 94k.
findings.quality: Needle 48213-KESTREL found at all three windows.
findings.caveat: Two rounds each; the difference is within noise.

findings.title: Saluki: a 2-bit Qwen3.8-27B that still calls tools
findings.summary: A 2-bit tune of Qwen3.8-27B (7.9 GB) passed test 1 with 72 tests and part-passed test 2, with 17 tools.
findings.quality: Graded by the standard test 1 and test 2 graders.
findings.caveat: Test 2 was partial (166 minutes at 22.0 tok/s); one run each.

findings.title: LFM2.5-24B is fast but passes no test 2
findings.summary: Five quants of LFM2.5-24B decoded at 125 to 176 tok/s on test 1 and passed it in three of five; none passed test 2.
findings.quality: Graded by the standard graders; test-2 servers had 0 to 3 tools.
findings.caveat: Test-1 runs were often two minutes long, so the test counts are small.

findings.title: Strata 0.1.44.1 doubles decode
findings.summary: Flash-Next on Strata, two rounds each: 0.1.44.1 loaded in a mean 60 s against 214 s, and decoded 44.9 tok/s against 18.3.
findings.quality: Same prompts and engine settings in all rounds.
findings.caveat: The first 0.1.42 round was cold; its warm round decoded 23.5 tok/s, so the true gain is nearer 1.9 times. Load time: 60 s against 214 s on the round mean, but the warm 0.1.42 round loaded in 41.5 s.

findings.title: Thinking models fail the one-shot pagoda
findings.summary: Qwen3.8-27B on vLLM with thinking on ran out of length in seven tries; with thinking off the three pages were blank.
findings.quality: Identical blank pages in the thinking-off tries.
findings.caveat: Other stacks also scored 0 on some tries: Tiel Coder one of five, Gemma-4-26B-A4B one of five, exllamav3 MTP five of six.

findings.title: Speed at 141k context
findings.summary: Four stacks timed on code with a 141k-token history: Gemma-4-26B-A4B with an MTP draft stays fastest, though it loses the most (54 %).
findings.quality: Needle found at 141k by all four.
findings.caveat: Prefill at that depth: 2,094, 2,046, 739 and about 650 tok/s.

findings.title: Engine shoot-out on Qwen3.8-27B
findings.summary: Drafting lifts decode from 42 tok/s to 95 to 170 tok/s on code; TensorFold with DFlash2 is fastest but holds the smallest window.
findings.quality: At temperature 0 drafting changed 7 of 15 exllamav3 DFlash2 replies, 10 of 15 with MTP, 4 of 15 on llama.cpp and none on TensorFold.
findings.caveat: The window with an 8-bit cache is 98k (exllamav3 DFlash2), 131k (MTP) and 43 to 73k (TensorFold). Baselines are each engine without drafting.

findings.title: Test 4: Tiel Coder fixes 9 of 9 tickets
findings.summary: Three tickets in a known-good Rust crate, three runs each: every run passed all hidden checks with no regressions and no false 'done'.
findings.quality: Hidden black-box checks (4, 11 and 13 per ticket) plus the crate's 155 tests; runs finished with 156 to 168 passing tests.
findings.caveat: One model only; the slowest run took 42 minutes.

findings.title: Old PCIe share doubles Flash-Next on Strata 0.1.42
findings.summary: Setting the old PCIe share on Strata 0.1.42 raised long-answer decode from 48 to 95 tok/s and big-prompt reads from 1,177 to 1,983 tok/s.
findings.quality: Test 1 passed in 51 minutes instead of 94; test 2 passed with 77 tests in 61 minutes instead of 98 (72 tests).
findings.caveat: Two probe rounds per variant; one agent run each.

findings.title: Grader audit changes four test-1 verdicts
findings.summary: All 125 archived test-1 and test-2 runs were regraded after fixing the graders; four test-1 verdicts changed.
findings.quality: Changes: Bonsai ada fail to pass, a Flash-Next row and a Qwen3.8 row partial to pass, Devstral Small 2 pass to partial.
findings.caveat: Twelve other rows had test counts corrected; six rows lost a no-crash tick.

findings.title: Maya patches take GLM-5.3-Flash to 19 tok/s
findings.summary: Two engine patches lifted decode from 3.95 to 18.7 tok/s; the model then passed test 1 (44 tests) and test 2 (7 tools, 66 tests, 322 minutes).
findings.caveat: Decode figures come from the run log, not a result file. A 1-bit variant failed both tests.

amend.title: An expert cache doubles Flash-Next on one 3090
amend.note: The 13 to 24 tok/s for orca is the best arm of the sweep. With the shipped config the streamed figure is about 19 tok/s (25 to 37 raw).
amend.caveat_add: The tqLLM control run measured the same GGUF at about 40 tok/s on short outputs; that measure is higher than the streamed one.

overall.tradeoff: Slower than the 27B stacks. The earlier build crashed under several sessions; the current stock builds served 11 of 11 sessions at about 25 tok/s on 2026-10-21, though no agent test has been rerun on them.
Gyro-S + MTP on Strata decodes 119 tok/s with a full test-2 pass in 24 minutes, but it is one run and Strata 0.2 is in beta.

best_per_test.evidence: 9 of 9 tickets, 84 of 84 hidden checks (only model tested)

best_per_test.model: lcpp6-tiel-coder-35b-t06, and as an agent qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-vllm and Coder 390
